site.name: Cachet
site.tagline: Batch PDF signing with the Belgian eID card
site.description: Sign a whole folder of PDFs with your Belgian eID card or an Azure Key Vault certificate. PAdES B-LTA by default: trusted timestamps, embedded revocation data and an archival chain — verified on the spot, never silently downgraded.

home.lead: Cachet signs a whole batch of PDFs in one pass — with your Belgian eID card, with your personal certificate in Azure Key Vault, or with a plain image stamp. Every cryptographic signature is PAdES, timestamped, long-term verifiable, and re-checked the moment it is written.

home.modesLead: Pick the mode that matches the legal weight the document needs.

sections.walkthrough: Signing a batch, step by step

overview.p1: Cachet is a batch PDF signer built for Belgian administrative workflows. You point it at a folder, choose how the documents should be signed, place the visible mark once, and it applies the same signature to every file in the batch.
overview.p2: It runs either as a step-by-step graphical wizard or as a console tool, from the same core. Cryptographic signatures follow the PAdES baseline standard (ETSI EN 319 142-1) up to level B-LTA: a trusted RFC 3161 timestamp, revocation data embedded in the document, and an archival timestamp chain — with trust anchors taken from the EU Trusted List for eID signatures, or from your organisation's internal CA for Azure signatures.
overview.p3: Every signed file is re-opened and validated immediately after writing, and the level actually achieved is reported. If the requested level cannot be reached, the document is marked failed. Cachet never silently produces a weaker signature than the one you asked for.
overview.quote: The eID mode uses the card's non-repudiation certificate, which is legally equivalent to a handwritten signature.

batch.title: Whole batches at once
batch.text: Point Cachet at files or folders. The same mark, page and position are applied to every document in the batch.

modes.title: Three signing modes
modes.text: A qualified eID signature, an advanced signature from Azure Key Vault, or a plain image stamp with no legal value.

pades.title: PAdES up to B-LTA
pades.text: Levels b-b, b-t, b-lt and b-lta, selectable per run. b-lta is the default — the strongest and longest-lasting.

timestamp.title: Trusted timestamping
timestamp.text: An RFC 3161 timestamp authority proves when you signed. Point it at a qualified TSA when eIDAS-qualified preservation matters.

ltv.title: Long-term validation
ltv.text: CA certificates and OCSP/CRL responses are embedded at signing time, so the PDF stays verifiable after the certificates expire.

verify.title: Verified on the spot
verify.text: Each signed file is re-opened and validated, and the achieved level is reported. Levels are never silently downgraded.

template.title: Template validation
template.text: Inputs are accepted only if their page count and per-page dimensions match a model PDF exactly. Rejected files are never signed.

placement.title: Click to place
placement.text: A real preview of the target page, rendered by the bundled PDFium engine. Click where the mark belongs — that is where it is signed.

vignette.title: Visible signature mark
vignette.text: eID signatures stamp the cardholder photo, name and date; Azure signatures stamp the name and date.

safety.title: Nothing overwritten
safety.text: Output is written as `{pattern}` in a folder you choose, and existing files are never replaced.

i18n.title: Six languages in the app
i18n.text: The wizard speaks English, French, Dutch, German, Spanish and Portuguese, and follows your system language by default.

standalone.title: Standalone binaries
standalone.text: One windowed app and one console tool per platform, for Linux and Windows. Nothing to install beyond the eID middleware.

modes.lead: All three modes stamp a visible mark and process the whole batch identically. What differs is the legal weight of what they produce.

beid.name: eID card
beid.requires: Card reader, eID card, one PIN per document
beid.note: The strongest legal weight, and the slowest for large batches — the PIN is requested for every document.

azure.name: Azure Key Vault
azure.requires: One Microsoft login per batch, a personal key and certificate in Key Vault
azure.note: Only the document digest is sent to Azure; the file itself never leaves your machine, and the private key never leaves the vault.

image.name: Image stamp
image.note: A visual mark only. It carries no legal value and proves nothing about who applied it.

walkthrough.lead: The graphical wizard walks through eight steps. A stepper marks completed steps green and problems red, contextual help sits beside every form, and switching language re-renders the current step without losing anything you entered.
walkthrough.cliNote: Prefer the console? The same batch runs as a single command — see the command line section below.

template.title: Choose a template
template.text: Pick a model PDF that every document in the batch should match. Signing a single document? Choose that document itself as the template.

documents.title: Add the documents
documents.text: Select individual files or whole folders. Folders are searched for PDFs automatically.

validation.title: Validate against the template
validation.text: Each file is checked for the same page count and exactly identical page dimensions. A pass/fail table shows the result, and rejected files are never signed. If some files have a different page count — scanned annexes appended, for instance — a selector appears so every file is signed on its own first or last page instead.

output.title: Choose an output folder
output.text: Signed files are written as `{pattern}`. Existing files are never overwritten; on a name collision, ` - 1`, ` - 2` and so on are appended.

type.title: Choose the signature type
type.text: eID, Azure or image, plus the PAdES level (b-lta by default). In Azure mode a panel collects the vault settings and offers a “Sign in with Microsoft” action. A “Full documentation” button opens this same reference inside the app.

placement.title: Place the mark
placement.text: The target page is rendered for real. Click where the mark should sit — in eID and Azure modes the visible vignette is signed exactly there. A manual page field is available, and when page counts differ the first/last selector appears here too.

signing.title: Sign
signing.text: A summary of everything chosen, a reminder to insert the eID card in eID mode, then progress as each document is signed. In eID mode the PIN is requested once per document; in Azure mode you signed in once for the whole batch.

report.title: Read the report
report.text: A per-document result table with the level actually achieved for each file — for example “PAdES-B-LTA, LTV ok” — and a button that opens the output folder.

walkthrough.welcomeAlt: The Cachet welcome screen, with the language selector and the Start button
walkthrough.shotNote: Screenshots are of the English interface; the wizard also speaks French, Dutch, German, Spanish and Portuguese.

cli.lead: The console tool shares its entire core with the wizard, so anything the interface can do is one command away. These examples assume a source checkout; with a downloaded build, replace the interpreter call with `cachet-cli`.
cli.flagsLead: The flags most runs need. The README documents the complete surface, including every Azure option.

examples.beid: Sign a folder with the eID card, at the default b-lta level
examples.offline: Sign offline at the basic level, with no network access
examples.image: Stamp an image, validated against a template
examples.azure: Sign with a personal Azure Key Vault certificate

flags.--gui: Launch the graphical interface; otherwise the tool runs in console mode.
flags.--input: Files and folders to process. Folders are searched for PDFs.
flags.--output: Output folder. Files are written as `{pattern}` and never overwritten.
flags.--template: Template PDF. When supplied, every input is validated against it.
flags.--page: Target page: a 1-based number, or `first` / `last` resolved per document.
flags.--x-y: Lower-left corner of the mark, in points from the bottom-left of the page. Omit both in eID mode for the bottom-right of the last page.
flags.--image-path: The image to stamp. Required in image mode.
flags.--timestamp-url: RFC 3161 timestamp authority for levels b-t and above.
flags.--azure-vault-url: Key Vault URL. Required in Azure mode.
flags.--azure-trust-anchors: PEM or DER file, or a directory, holding the internal CA chain used as LTV trust anchors in Azure mode.
flags.--refresh-trust-list: Force a re-download of the EU trusted list, bypassing the 24-hour cache.

levels.lead: PAdES baseline levels, as defined by ETSI EN 319 142-1. Each builds on the one before it, and Cachet defaults to the strongest.

adds.b-b: The basic signature: who signed, and that nothing changed since
adds.b-t: A trusted RFC 3161 timestamp, proving when
adds.b-lt: Revocation data and CA certificates embedded in the document (LTV)
adds.b-lta: An archival timestamp chain, so the evidence itself keeps proving out

requirements.lead: What each mode needs at runtime.

beid.title: eID mode
items: The Belgian eID middleware, which provides the PKCS#11 library
A card reader with an eID card inserted
Network access for levels b-t and above; b-b is fully offline

azure.title: Azure mode
items: Outbound access to login.microsoftonline.com and your Key Vault URL
A personal key and certificate provisioned in Key Vault by an administrator
Reachable CRL or OCSP endpoints on the internal CA for levels b-lt and above

image.title: Image mode
items: Nothing — pure PDF stamping, fully offline

requirements.preview: The page preview in the placement step needs nothing extra: the PDFium rendering engine is bundled with the application.

install.lead: Two ways in: download a standalone build, or run it from source.
install.binaryText: Download the archive for your platform and extract it. It contains a windowed application and a console tool, both self-contained — no Python installation required. The eID middleware remains a separate runtime requirement for eID signing, and is never bundled.
install.sourceText: Clone the repository, create a virtual environment and install the dependencies. On Debian and Ubuntu the graphical interface also needs the system Tk package.
install.buildText: Native Linux, native Windows, cross-building through Wine and the GitHub Actions pipeline are all documented in BUILD.md.

reference.title: Reference
reference.lead: The sections below are the application's own reference documentation, reproduced word for word so the site and the app never say different things.
reference.notTranslated: This reference is not yet available in your language; it is shown in English.

rrn.title: Your national register number is in every eID signature
rrn.text: The Belgian eID non-repudiation certificate contains your national register number (RRN), and that certificate is embedded in every signature it produces. Anyone who receives a signed PDF can read it. Cachet warns about this at startup and in its summary — think about how the signed documents will be distributed.

tsa.title: Free timestamps are not qualified timestamps
tsa.text: The default timestamp authority is free and produces technically valid B-T and B-LTA signatures, but not qualified timestamps in the eIDAS sense. For genuine qualified long-term preservation, point the timestamp URL at a qualified authority — the EU trusted list identifies providers offering qualified timestamping services.

aes.title: Azure signatures are advanced, not qualified
aes.text: Azure mode produces an advanced electronic signature (AES). That is appropriate for internal documents, but it is one tier below the qualified signature (QES) the eID card produces. For documents relied on by external third parties, a publicly recognised qualified issuer would be needed.

archival.title: B-LTA chains need renewing
archival.text: The archival timestamp chain keeps the evidence provable over time, but for genuine long-term archival that chain has to be renewed periodically. BUILD.md explains what that involves.
